science.headline:
How IV Therapy
Differs From Vitamin Pills
science.body: When you swallow vitamin pills, your stomach breaks them down first. IV therapy delivers nutrients directly into your bloodstream, supporting hydration and nutrient levels.
bullets: Delivered directly into the bloodstream. This does not guarantee absorption or clinical benefit.
Compounded fresh & prescribed by licensed medical doctors
Administered by registered nurses in a relaxing clinic suite

cards.title: Bypasses Stomach Breakdown
cards.detail: IV drips bypass digestion so nutrients enter your bloodstream directly.

cards.title: Direct Vascular Delivery
cards.detail: Intravenous drips deliver nutrients directly into your bloodstream.

myths.reality: No. Our experienced registered nurses use tiny needles and gentle techniques so you barely feel a pinch. You can relax, read, or watch TV during your drip.
No. Oral vitamins must pass through digestion first, while IV drips deliver nutrients directly into your bloodstream for hydration and nutrient support.

Every drip is prescribed by a licensed doctor and administered by trained registered nurses. IV therapy carries risks, such as infection, vein irritation or allergic reaction, which your provider will discuss with you. Some formulations are compounded and are not FDA-approved.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor's consultation before getting an IV drip?
faqs.answer: Yes. All IV vitamin infusions are prescribed medical treatments. You will complete a quick health review with our licensed medical doctor so your drip can be customized to you.

faqs.question: What does the doctor-guided IV program include?
faqs.answer: Your program includes a medical consultation, custom compounded IV vitamins prepared fresh, comfortable seating in our luxury medical suite, and professional administration by registered nurses.

faqs.question: How long does an IV drip session take?
faqs.answer: Most standard IV vitamin drips take 30 to 45 minutes, allowing your body to absorb every drop comfortably.

faqs.question: How often should I get IV vitamin therapy?
faqs.answer: Most wellness patients visit once or twice a month for high energy and immune health. Active athletes or those recovering from illness often get weekly drips.

faqs.question: How are IV infusions supervised?
faqs.answer: All infusions are prescribed by licensed doctors, prepared by a pharmacy, and administered by trained registered nurses. IV therapy carries risks, and your provider will review them with you. Some formulations are compounded and are not FDA-approved.

faqs.question: How do I get started with IV therapy?
faqs.answer: Getting started is simple! Call our clinic today at (727) 476-8966 or click 'Book Your Doctor Consultation' online. Our medical team will prepare your custom drip!

faqs.question: Is glutathione IV therapy FDA-approved?
faqs.answer: Glutathione given by IV or injection at wellness clinics is generally compounded by a pharmacy, and compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Research on glutathione IVs in healthy adults is limited, so your provider reviews your history, medications and goals before recommending it and explains what to expect. Results vary.
